sourceRenderMethod.howTheSourceWasRendered: pdftoppm -r 600 -gray -png, Poppler 24.02.0, WITH ANNOTATIONS DRAWN. -hide-annotations was never passed on any measuring render, so the source render carries the widget /AP /N appearance ink whose absence from a delivered page the directional difference exists to detect. The delivered fixtures carry no AcroForm at all (pdfinfo Form: none; a pdf-lib enumeration returns 0 widgets), so every mark on a delivered page is content-stream ink and the annotation question arises only on the source side.
sourceRenderMethod.provenAtWholePageLevel: Pinned 600-00228 rendered both ways in this container at 600 dpi, grey<128: page 1 reads 1611695 dark with annotations against 1602354 with -hide-annotations (net 9341); page 2 reads 1236377 against 1231064 (net 5313).
sourceRenderMethod.provenAtWidgetLevelAndStrongerThanACrop: The net figure is not trusted, and it is not the whole truth: it is the difference of two directional counts. Decomposing the annotations-on / annotations-off difference onto EVERY source widget rectangle on the page (not four hand-picked 132x132 crops) gives, on page 1: annotations ADD 14085 dark pixels and COVER 4744, and 14085 = 3791 (f21) + 3688 (f22) + 3655 (f16) + 2951 (f15) and 4744 = 1178 + 1536 + 947 + 1083 exactly, with gain 0 and loss 0 OUTSIDE every widget rectangle on the page. Page 2: annotations add 7479 = 3791 (f72) + 3688 (f73) and cover 2166 = 1083 + 1083, again 0 and 0 outside every widget rect. A render that failed to draw /AP /N would have shown these as zero; a render drawing something else would have left a remainder outside the rects. There is no remainder.
sourceRenderMethod.thresholdSweptNotAssumed: Thresholds 96,104,112,120,128,136,144,160 at 600 dpi. The annotation gain is 14085 (p1) / 7479 (p2) at EVERY threshold in that range; the annotation loss is stable at 4744 / 2166 across 112-144. t=128 sits inside both plateaus and every figure in these rows is published at grey<128, 600 dpi unless stated.
sourceRenderMethod.thresholded: grayscale < 128 counted as dark; ADDED = dark in delivered and not in source, REMOVED = dark in source and not in delivered, reported PER PAGE.
sourceRenderMethod.whatTheAnnotationLossMeans: 4744 pixels on page 1 and 2166 on page 2 are dark WITHOUT annotations and light WITH them: the six selection widgets’ source-authored /AP /N /Off appearances paint over the court’s own printed ballot-box outline and redraw it. That is the source’s own behaviour, it is what a PDF viewer shows a participant, and it is the reason FIX130’s single net figure of 9341 understates what the annotation layer does. Reporting one net number for this page hides a 4744-pixel directional loss.
sourceRenderMethod.intermediatesDeleted: Every 600 and 300 dpi PNG rendered by this lane was deleted immediately after it was counted. None is left on disk and none is committed.

theHeadline.theMethodIRanIndependently: For each widget on the pinned 600-00228 I paired the widget rectangle with the printed dollar run whose baseline falls INSIDE that rectangle and overlaps it in x; I took the column from the page’s two printed headings by x-position (41.64 for the income column, 320.40 for the expenses column) and never from extraction order; and I read the caption from the printed items on that run’s own baseline band, inside that run’s own column, to the left of the run. A widget with no such run, or with more than one, would have been refused rather than guessed.
theHeadline.theOrphanTrapWasAvoided: FIX130 records that a detector testing for an item whose whole text is exactly "$" silently orphaned four widgets, because the income column encodes its marker differently. My run predicate accepts any item beginning with a dollar sign, and the result is that 21 widgets on page 1 each paired with exactly one run and none was orphaned: 7 in the income column and 14 in the expenses column. No widget was ambiguous.
theHeadline.theResult: All 21 pairings match the delivered disclosureLabel. In the expenses column, reading down: f45 Rent or Mortgage Payment, f46 Electric Service, f47 Phone, f48 Fuel (heat and/or gas), f49 Food, f50 Clothing, f51 Medical, f52 Child Support, f53 Auto Loan Payment, f54 Property Taxes, f55 Insurance (health, auto, etc.), f56 Other Expenses, f57 Total Expenses.
theHeadline.theVF03Defect: f57 is the blank beside the printed words "Total Expenses" - the run at y=56.59 sits inside f57’s rect y=[50.56,62.86] and the caption on that run’s baseline band in its own column is "Total Expenses". It is disclosed as "Total Expenses" with the what-to-write "the total of your monthly expenses". The defect on which VF03 returned fifteen-of-fifteen - f57 disclosed as "Other Expenses" with "any other monthly expense" on a declaration signed under penalty of perjury - is repaired, and "Other Expenses" now sits correctly on f56 one row above.
theHeadline.field35: The other corrected caption I could falsify and could not. f35 rect y=[136.43,147.42] contains exactly one run, at y=141.36, whose baseline band carries the printed continuation line of the Other Income parenthetical. The line the old label named, "Self-Employment/Business Income", is printed at y=119.19 - 17 points BELOW the bottom of f35’s rectangle, so f35 cannot be its blank. The delivered label names the italic line under Other Income, which is where the blank is.
theHeadline.theTwoLeftAsCommitted: MonthlyTotal and f41. FIX130 recorded these as genuinely ambiguous with two of three signals supporting the committed pairing. I measure them as decided, and decided the same way: MonthlyTotal’s rect y=[93.56,104.56] contains the run at y=99.2 AND the printed caption "Total Monthly Income" at y=94.63, while the competing line "(other than wages)" at y=107.39 lies outside the rectangle; f41’s rect y=[80.91,91.90] contains the run at 86.96 and the caption at 82.39. Rect, run and the widget’s own name MonthlyTotal all agree. The consequence, which the form and not the packet owns, is that the printed line "Self-Employment/Business Income (other than wages)" has no blank of its own, and the item list correctly contains no entry for it.

WHAT DISTINGUISHES THEM FOR THE PARTICIPANT: only the guide, and there substantially - five different files, each carrying its own statutory subsection, its own waiting period (three years under Sec. 7602(c), seven under (d), ten under (e), thirty days under Sec. 7609), its own exclusion list and its own stop-and-get-a-lawyer list. DOES THE DISTINCTION REACH THE DELIVERED PACKET: no, not one byte of it. IS THAT A DEFECT: on the evidence, no, and I tested the question rather than assuming either way. The Alabama precedent in the record is a clone whose pardoned family left unticked eight eligibility boxes its own CR-65 Section V required. Vermont has no equivalent: 200-00130 is a single statewide petition whose only twelve selection widgets are factual questions about the participant’s record, and NOT ONE of them encodes the statutory ground, so there is no route-specific value for any of the five to have written and left unwritten. The identical filing is a property of the Vermont Judiciary’s form, not of these packets. It remains a governance question for the Captain - five commercially distinct routes selling one identical PDF - and I raise it as such rather than settling it.
